description: About Etched Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history. Job Summary We are seeking talented Spring ‘27 and Summer ‘27 IA Research Engineer interns to build the agents that accelerate how Etched produces frontier tokens. You will embed with our kernels team and work alongside our founders on agentic harnesses, tools, and evals that let agents do long-running engineering work people actually rely on. This role is for builders who thrive on ambiguity, have real product sense, and want to own problems end to end. Key responsibilities Embed with our kernels team to find high-leverage bottlenecks and help turn them into tools engineers use every day. Build and deploy LLM agents wired into our engineering workflows via tool-calling and MCP. Help build execution environments where agents can verify their own work, with sandboxed access to simulators, compilers, profilers, and real hardware. Ship internal products end to end, including the interfaces, data pipelines, and infrastructure behind them. Design evals and track adoption to measure which tools are working and which aren’t. Support special projects with the founders across the company. You may be a good fit if you have Progress towards a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field Strong software engineering fundamentals and a record of shipping projects other people use Built agents for multi-step tasks beyond calling an API: tool design, context management, evals, and failure analysis Heavy use of coding agents, including reading their transcripts and changing the system when an agent is confidently wrong High agency in unfamiliar domains, product sense, and extreme attention to detail Strong candidates may have some experience with Chip development, GPU kernels, hardware, or manufacturing Infrastructure, data engineering, or DevOps Fine-tuning, RAG over technical data, or multi-agent orchestration Hackathons, startups, or side projects with real users We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification. Program details 12-week paid internship Daily lunch and dinner in our office Based at our office in San Jose, CA Direct mentorship from industry leaders and world-class engineers Opportunity to work on one of the most important problems of our time For any questions, contact internships@etched.com. How we’re different Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors. We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

description: About us Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia. We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do. Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor . Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace. Sierra’s Applied Research team works to make the models behind our agents better, faster, and cheaper across many kinds of tasks. Our work covers post-training open-weight models for specialized capabilities, new approaches to voice AI, and the benchmarks the field uses to measure agents, including τ-bench. As an Applied Research Intern, you’ll join the team for a research project, working with a mentor, you’ll pick a problem that matters to how AI agents perform in the real world, run rigorous experiments, and potentially write up what you find for a top venue. If you want your research to reach both the research community and production agents used by millions of people, come do it at Sierra. What you’ll do Own a research project from start to finish, from framing the question and running experiments to writing and submitting a paper. Push agent evaluation forward, for example by extending τ-bench to new domains, modalities, or long-horizon tasks, or by building new ways to measure reliability and consistency. Study how agents reason, use tools, and follow policies over multi-turn conversations, and find out where and why they fail. Explore post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior, and measure the gains rigorously. Work with large-scale, proprietary datasets of text and audio interactions to find research questions grounded in real customer problems. Work with researchers and engineers across Sierra, and where it makes sense, turn your findings into improvements in production. What you’ll bring Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field. A research track record, such as first-author publications or submissions at venues like NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, Interspeech or ICASSP. Strong experimental skills: you design clean experiments, build careful baselines, and are honest about what the results do and do not show. Fluency in Python and modern ML tooling (for example, PyTorch, and LLM inference and training stacks). High agency and a builder’s mindset. You’ll work across the stack to get an experiment running. Clear, direct communication, both in writing and when presenting research. Even better Research experience with LLM agents, tool use, or multi-turn dialogue. Experience designing benchmarks or evaluations, especially ones tied to real-world outcomes. Experience with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or long-horizon optimization. Experience with speech, voice, or multimodal models. Open-source contributions to ML research code or benchmarks. Intern qualifications The internship is open to students currently enrolled in a PhD program. Duration and start dates are flexible. Interns are embedded with the Applied Research team and work under the guidance of a mentor. The internship is based in our San Francisco office. We are in person Monday through Thursday. Our values Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work. Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it. Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve. Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time. Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements. What we offer We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees: Flexible (unlimited) paid time off Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family Life insurance and disability benefits Retirement plan dependent on country of employment Parental leave Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized Discretionary

description: Wheeled Platforms & Lifting Systems Emeryville, California | Internship Proposed base compensation. Final terms are subject to Astera’s hiring process. About Astera Astera Institute is a private foundation supporting ambitious work in science and technology through grants, investments, and in-house research. Its research programs combine the pace and autonomy of a startup with the freedom to pursue difficult scientific questions. Learn more about Astera’s mission at astera.org/vision . About the Robotics Lab We are building a frontier robotics lab at Astera Institute. We believe neuroscience and AI will converge in embodied intelligence: animals and robots face shared challenges of perceiving their surroundings, navigating, manipulating objects, and using memory and reasoning to accomplish tasks in the physical world. Robotics provides a powerful testbed for investigating how biological neural circuits solve these challenges and for developing AI systems that turn perception, learning, and cognition into effective action. Our strategy starts with making robots useful, while developing a mechanistic understanding of how neural circuits can generate intelligent behavior. We aim to continually expand the repertoire of behaviors a robot can perform reliably in real environments, while improving its ability to learn new skills, adapt to changing conditions, and recover from failure. These practical capabilities provide both measurable outcomes and a foundation for investigating deeper principles of intelligence. Wheeled robotic platforms are one of the embodiments we use to test neural-circuit models and AI systems as we work toward general embodied intelligence. We have already demonstrated indoor navigation on a simple differential-drive platform. We are now expanding this work to evaluate other wheel and drivetrain configurations, along with lifting systems that allow robots to adjust their working height. Position Summary Help us build and compare the systems that allow robots to move and adjust their working height. Under engineering mentorship, you will prototype wheeled mobile bases and lifting platforms, run hands-on experiments, and evaluate how different designs perform under realistic operating conditions. Starting with our existing hoverboard hub motors and other motorized wheel hardware, you will help explore different wheel and drivetrain configurations. You will also help develop and evaluate lifting platforms, comparing commercially available mechanisms and custom prototypes. Your work will help the team select practical designs based on measured performance, reliability, cost, and ease of integration. Core Responsibilities Evaluate wheeled platforms. Assemble and modify mobile bases using hoverboard hub motors, hub motor wheels, and conventional motor-driven wheel assemblies. Help design and fabricate chassis, mounts, and supporting components. Compare navigation performance of different systems. Compare wheel and drivetrain configurations. Develop repeatable tests to evaluate maneuverability, low-speed motion, traction, payload handling, power consumption, steerability and general performance across relevant floor surfaces. Prototype lifting platforms. Help assemble, adapt, and test different lifting mechanisms, such as scissor lifts and telescoping lifting columns. Integrate actuators, guides, mounts, and supporting structures. Evaluate lifting performance. Compare lifting range, speed, positioning repeatability, rigidity, and stability under defined loads. Investigate vibration, mechanical play, and other issues that affect reliable operation. Integrate controls and measurements. Configure motor controllers, connect position and speed feedback, and develop simple control and data-collection scripts. Help implement travel limits, homing, and coordinated motion under engineering supervision. Document comparisons and improve designs. Maintain CAD files, wiring diagrams, parts lists, and test records. Summarize tradeoffs and work with engineers to refine promising designs. Keep experimental hardware ready. Organize components, tools, and spares; maintain prototypes and test fixtures; and assist with equipment inspections, repairs, and experiment setup. Required Qualifications Coursework, projects, or practical experience in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, robotics, mechatronics, or a related discipline. Experience building and troubleshooting a physical system through coursework, research, student teams, or personal projects. Basic familiarity with mechanical assembly, electrical wiring, motors, and sensors. Interest in hands-on prototyping and systematic testing, including careful measurement and documentation. Comfort working with an engineering mentor and contributing to the upkeep of a shared robotics lab. Preferred Experience CAD, 3D printing, machining, or fabrication of mechanical prototypes. BLDC motors, motor controllers, encoders, wheeled robots, or drivetrain design. Linear actuators, screw drives, scissor lifts, lifting columns, or other positioning mechanisms. Python, C/C++, microcontrollers, or basic feedback control. Building test fixtures, collecting experimental data, or comparing hardware designs. Prior experience with every technology listed is not expected. We value curiosity, practical problem-solving, and an interest in understanding how different mechanical systems perform through real experiments.

Parspec applies AI to power workflows that help stakeholders evaluate products, surface better options, and act with confidence. You enjoy breaking down complex systems, working with imperfect data, and experimenting to find practical solutions. description: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. Role Overview REGENT's Viceroy and Squire Seagliders rely on actuators and drive systems that have to perform flawlessly in a demanding, real-world environment, and getting them there starts in the lab. As an Actuation Engineering Intern , you'll work alongside our actuation engineering team to build test setups, run evaluations, and dig into vendor documentation to assess how different actuators and drives stack up against each other. You'll spend real time with real hardware, installing actuators on test stands, building jigs, and generating the data that directly informs which components earn a place on our Seaglider product line. This role sits within our Electrical Systems team, part of Engineering & Technology, where hands-on rigor and clear-eyed evaluation matter as much as clever design. You'll be given increasing independence as the term goes on, moving from guided lab work to running your own experiments and assembling findings into a presentation that will genuinely shape the actuation approach for Viceroy and Squire. If you've got your engineering fundamentals down and are looking for a chance to apply them to real test hardware on a team that's reinventing coastal transportation, you'll feel right at home here. What You'll Do Build Real Test Setups: You'll construct test stands and jigs in the actuation lab, installing actuators and drives and getting hands-on with the hardware that powers our Seagliders. Evaluate Actuators and Drives: You'll run performance evaluations on actuators and drive systems, comparing them against similar models to understand tradeoffs and capabilities. Dig Into Vendor Documentation: You'll interpret datasheets and manuals and work directly with vendors to understand product specifications and communication requirements. Talk to the Hardware: You'll use programming tools like Python to communicate with actuators and drives, pulling data and verifying behavior firsthand. Support Qualification Work: You'll help qualify actuators and drives for service on Viceroy and Squire, contributing evidence-based assessments that inform real engineering decisions. Work With Assemblies and CAD: You'll navigate CAD models and help arrange actuation equipment within assemblies as part of your evaluation work. Present Your Findings: You'll compile the results of your assessments into a presentation for the mechanical and electrical teams, directly shaping the actuation approach used across our product line. What You'll Bring Engineering Fundamentals in Place: You're a rising senior or grad student in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, mechatronics engineering, or a related field, with the core fundamentals already solid. Comfort With Hand Tools: You're mechanically inclined and comfortable working with hand tools, building jigs, and handling hardware constantly. Basic Programming Ability: You have working knowledge of a language like Python, enough to communicate with actuators and drives and make sense of the data they produce. Clear Communicator: You write and speak clearly, including when working with outside vendors to interpret datasheets and learn about new products. Bonus: Actuator or Sensor Experience: Prior hands-on exposure to actuators, communication protocols, or sensors such as temperature, force, strain, or position would give you a real head start in this niche domain. Bonus: CAD and Circuits Know-How: Experience with 3D CAD and drawings, and comfort working with low-voltage DC power circuits, means less time spent learning the basics and more time in the lab. Bonus: MATLAB/Simulink Exposure: Familiarity with MATLAB or Simulink is a plus, since it's key software for post-processing actuator data and modeling actuation systems. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. Creative Problem Solver : You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. description: About us Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia. We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do. Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor . Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace. Sierra’s Applied Research team works to make the models behind our agents better, faster, and cheaper across many kinds of tasks. Our work covers post-training open-weight models for specialized capabilities, new approaches to voice AI, and the benchmarks the field uses to measure agents, including τ-bench. As an Applied Research Intern, you’ll join the team for a research project, working with a mentor, you’ll pick a problem that matters to how AI agents perform in the real world, run rigorous experiments, and potentially write up what you find for a top venue. If you want your research to reach both the research community and production agents used by millions of people, come do it at Sierra. What you’ll do Own a research project from start to finish, from framing the question and running experiments to writing and submitting a paper. Push agent evaluation forward, for example by extending τ-bench to new domains, modalities, or long-horizon tasks, or by building new ways to measure reliability and consistency. Study how agents reason, use tools, and follow policies over multi-turn conversations, and find out where and why they fail. Explore post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior, and measure the gains rigorously. Work with large-scale, proprietary datasets of text and audio interactions to find research questions grounded in real customer problems. Work with researchers and engineers across Sierra, and where it makes sense, turn your findings into improvements in production. What you’ll bring Currently pursuing a PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field. A research track record, such as first-author publications or submissions at venues like NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, Interspeech or ICASSP. Strong experimental skills: you design clean experiments, build careful baselines, and are honest about what the results do and do not show. Fluency in Python and modern ML tooling (for example, PyTorch, and LLM inference and training stacks). High agency and a builder’s mindset. You’ll work across the stack to get an experiment running. Clear, direct communication, both in writing and when presenting research. Even better Research experience with LLM agents, tool use, or multi-turn dialogue. Experience designing benchmarks or evaluations, especially ones tied to real-world outcomes. Experience with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, or long-horizon optimization. Experience with speech, voice, or multimodal models. Open-source contributions to ML research code or benchmarks. Intern qualifications The internship is open to students currently enrolled in a PhD program. Duration and start dates are flexible. Interns are embedded with the Applied Research team and work under the guidance of a mentor. The internship is based in our San Francisco office. We are in person Monday through Thursday. Our values Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work. Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it. Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve. Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time. Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements. description: About Taara: Born at X, Google's Moonshot Factory, Taara is on a mission to connect billions of people lacking abundant and affordable internet today by pioneering the way we use light to deliver faster, cheaper, more reliable connectivity. We are bringing groundbreaking wireless optical communication and photonics chip technologies to the world to bridge the digital divide. Joining Taara allows you to work as part of a multidisciplinary team of experts in optics, software, and hardware, all collaborating to solve the hardest connectivity challenges on a global scale. If you want to tackle problems that matter and build tools with real-world impact, we would love to meet you. About the Role: As an Optical PLL Research Intern , you will lay the groundwork for an integrated optical phase-locked loop (OPLL) that locks an external laser for coherent reception in next-generation wireless optical links. This is a long-term project spanning lab and simulation, ideally a year or more. It could also anchor a thesis or a longer-term collaboration. What such a loop can achieve is bounded by real components. You will evaluate lasers, modulators, and analog electronics, build benchtop experiments around them, and work toward a stable closed loop. In parallel, you will extend our simulation and use the two to check each other. There is genuine room to shape the direction. Survey what is available, design your own experiments, and follow the evidence to the strongest design. How you will make 10X Impact: Component Evaluation: Screen commercial lasers, modulators, and photodetectors. Measure what vendors do not publish. Loop Design: Design the loops that track carrier phase and frequency, and validate them against control theory. Chip Requirements: Define what the integrated OPLL needs from its laser, electronics, and loop. Physical-Layer Simulation: Extend our model of the link and reconcile it with measurement. What you should have: Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, Optics, Communications, or a related field. A strong background in analog and RF electronics and circuit design , including noise, bandwidth, and delay analysis. Hands-on lab experience with lasers, modulators, photodetectors , and high-speed test equipment. Control theory applied on hardware: closing feedback loops and diagnosing oscillation, drift, or loss of lock. Working knowledge of digital communications and signal processing . Availability of at least 6 months, ideally 12 or more, and three days per week in the Sunnyvale office. It'd be great if you also had one or more of these: Laser Locking: Frequency stabilization, tunable sources, phase-locked loops, carrier recovery, or coherent detection. Photodetection & Front-End Electronics: Photoreceiver, TIA, or high-speed circuit design. Numerical Methods: Scientific Python (NumPy, SciPy, JAX), phase-noise modeling, or cycle-slip statistics. Domain Knowledge: Optical or RF communications, photonics, or fading channels. What we offer: Competitive salary: $7,000–$10,000/month depending on degree. Flexible duration to fit your academic schedule. Direct mentorship from industry-leading engineers in a "moonshot" environment. Opportunity to work on technology that has the potential to change how billions of people access the internet.

description: At Upvest, we are on a mission to make investing as easy as spending money . Upvest empowers businesses to offer a wide range of investment products and the best experience in the field of capital market investment and retirement planning. Upvest’s Investment API is easy to integrate so that fintechs and financial institutions can save resources and fully focus on their core business. We are proud to partner with Europe’s leading Fintechs and financial institutions such as DKB, Revolut, N26 and Raisin. Founded in 2017 by Martin Kassing, Upvest now brings together over 270 talented professionals from more than 70 nationalities. Upvest is backed by €280M in total funding from world-class investors, including BlackRock, Tencent, Sapphire Ventures, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Earlybird, Notion Capital, and Motive . Our latest €105M funding round in March 2026 - led by Sapphire and Tencent - serves as a massive catalyst for our growth, allowing us to offer premier investment experience. About the role: As a Brokerage Operations Intern you will dive into the fast-paced world of capital markets. You will support our Brokerage Managers in daily trading activities, risk management, order monitoring, and the operational rollout of exciting new investment products. This is a unique opportunity to learn the intricacies of trade execution, algorithmic trading, and investment management from industry experts. What you’ll do: Order Management & Best Execution: Support the daily monitoring of trade executions and order flows to help ensure client trades are processed accurately, on time, and in strict adherence to best execution policies. Risk Management & Algorithmic Trading Support: Assist the team in monitoring algorithmic trading flows and evaluating daily operational risks, helping to ensure our automated trading systems run smoothly and within defined risk parameters. Market Abuse Monitoring & Compliance: Support the continuous monitoring of trading activities to assist in identifying potential market abuse scenarios. Help prepare data for regulatory compliance reporting (such as MiFIR, MAR, or Best Execution). Investment Universe Management: Assist in managing and expanding our offered investment universe across various European and EMEA jurisdictions, ensuring new and existing assets align with local regulatory and operational requirements. Trade Execution Support: Assist with the daily operational processes surrounding trading, including the execution handling for equities, mutual funds, and ELTIFs (European Long-Term Investment Funds). Product Planning & Launch: Collaborate cross-functionally with Product and Operations teams to assist with research and operational readiness for new brokerage product launches across different regions. Ad-Hoc Brokerage Projects: Actively participate in team projects aimed at improving execution mechanisms, rectifying mistrades, and optimizing our internal trading infrastructure. What you bring: Keen Interest in Markets & Data: A strong, demonstrable passion for financial markets, data analysis, trading, and the fintech ecosystem. Foundational Knowledge: Basic understanding of market structures, trade lifecycles, and different financial instruments (knowledge of mutual funds, ELTIFs, or algorithmic trading concepts is a great bonus!). Analytical Mindset: High attention to detail, excellent problem-solving skills, and a proactive, "hands-on" attitude when dealing with complex data. Tech-Savvy: Comfortable working with data and eager to learn about trading platforms, market data tools (like Bloomberg), and internal order management systems. Communication: Fluency in English is required; German is a strong plus. How we Upvest in you: Impact-driven work: We’re building the infrastructure that will power the future of investing in Europe. It’s complex, ambitious, and meaningful. You’ll work with modern technologies and create something entirely new. No legacy systems, no limits. Team celebrations: Participate in company-wide events, such as UpFest, dinners, offsites and our Holiday party, to connect with colleagues and celebrate our achievements. Inclusion : We’re committed to a culture where everyone belongs and thrives. Our Employee Resources Groups foster inclusion and connection, like Upfem for our female Upvengers, or UpVergent supporting neurodivergent Upvengers and allies. Our Values: Make it easy for others. We simplify the complex and act with the best intentions. Own the outcome. We are proactive, fast and confident to get the job done, valuing progress over perfection. Rise to the challenge. We aim high and push the boundaries. We stay curious, learn and celebrate our wins together. Tell the story. We start with the Why to align on purpose. We are transparent and share knowledge to empower and inspire others. Upvest is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

description:
The ACLU seeks a Legal Intern in the National Political Advocacy Department of the ACLU’s National office in Washington, DC. This internship is part-time and hybrid.

Qualifying applicants must currently be matriculated undergraduate students or an equivalent combination of education and/or experience and must be based in the U.S. for the entire duration of the internship.

 

The Team:

The National Political Advocacy Department (NPAD) works to strengthen the efforts of the ACLU at the federal, state, and local levels of government. The department harnesses the political power that comes from having more than eight million members and supporters, as well as affiliates in every state. By organizing grassroots lobbying and issue campaigns using modern tactics, the ACLU seeks to continue to achieve change as profound in the legislative, administrative and electoral arenas as it accomplishes through the courts.  

The Democracy and Technology Policy & Government Affairs team is made up of eight members, including seven attorneys, who work with Congress, state legislatures, regulatory agencies and others to strengthen and protect rights to voting, free speech, and privacy; to advance racial justice; and to ensure that emerging technologies (in artificial intelligence, algorithmic decision-making, and surveillance) are not used to deny rights or discriminate.

What You’ll Do:

The intern will work on legal and policy research and writing-related projects centered on voting, racial justice, free speech, technology policy, or democracy reform. They will assist members of our team with researching and analyzing legislation, elected officials, coalition partners, and relevant developments in the political and advocacy landscapes on the state and federal levels. They will help prepare advocacy and public education materials, correspondence, and reports as needed. They will also support our team's efforts to do congressional outreach through the form of briefings, meetings on Capitol Hill, and letters.

Your Day to Day

About Agoda

At Agoda, we bridge the world through travel. Our story began in 2005, when two lifelong friends and entrepreneurs, driven by their passion for travel, launched Agoda to make it easier for everyone to explore the world.  

 

Today, we are part of Booking Holdings [NASDAQ: BKNG], with a diverse team of over 7,000 people from 90 countries, working together in offices around the globe. Every day, we connect people to destinations and experiences, with our great deals across our millions of hotels and holiday properties, flights, and experiences worldwide.

 

No two days are the same at Agoda. Data and technology are at the heart of our culture, fueling our curiosity and innovation. If you’re ready to begin your best journey and help build travel for the world, join us.

Cooperative internship period: January - May 2027

Get to know our team:  

The Security Department oversees security, compliance, GRC, and security operations for all Agoda. We are vigilant in ensuring there is no breach or vulnerability threatening our company or endangering our employees in order to keep Agoda safe and protected. This would be a great challenge for those who want to work with the best technology in a dynamic and advanced environment.

The opportunity: 

Agoda’s IT-Security team is looking for fast learner and a highly motivated Security Analyst Intern looking to jumpstart their career in an exciting, highly rewarding IT-security domain. You will work for IT-security team at Agoda helping in keeping the company secure by keeping the bad guys out. You will get the opportunity to work, collaborate and learn from experienced IT-security defenders and help create a safer Agoda by protecting against internal and external attacks. You bring the basics and motivation, and we will take care of your training and education. If you like to learn new things every day, apply and work with us.

In this role, you'll get to:

  • Learn how to use security tools such as EDR, Email security, network security to track, analyse, contain, and flush out attackers from the network.
  • Assist with daily activities and functions of the security team to help update and maintain documents, policies, procedures
  • Learn to read and analyze log data to identify suspicious patterns and identify potential security threats
  • Provide first level security alert monitoring and contribute to triaging security investigations.
  • Analyze phishing emails and learn how attackers work and how to identify their traces in the company
  • Automate repetitive tasks that help speed up triaging security incidents
  • Assist in building security awareness training material and documenting security incidents
  • Participate in investigating large scale security incidents in a fast moving, agile environment

What you'll need to succeed:

  • Currently pursuing a degree in computer science, IT or a related field of study
  • Fundamentals of IT security, good knowledge of Windows and Linux operating systems and networking
  • Enthusiasm to build a career and learn something new every day in the domain of cyber defense and IT security
  • Fluency in written and spoken English

It's great if you have: 

  • Good programming skills in any language of your choice.
  • Experience in log analysis, using security tools or keen interest in cyber security
  • Exposure to concepts of networking, cyber security via formal education in university or self-learned.
  • Ability to work in a high pace, fast moving environment
  • Familiarity with agentic AI coding tools such as Cursor, Codex, Claude Code, or Grok.

Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. 

With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization.

Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA.

Embedded Software Developer, Network/Payload Software Intern (Winter 2027)

Internships at Astranis typically last for twelve weeks, and are hourly roles designed for students who are currently enrolled at a four-year university. 

As an Intern, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems — we pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on challenging projects, no matter their seniority. Many past interns have designed and tested hardware/software that is heading to space on our first satellite, and many of them are now full-time employees at Astranis. 

Role

  • Work with engineering teams across disciplines to design, prototype, develop and test software for both space vehicles and ground infrastructure
  • Develop software for custom built PCBs and industry standard satellite communications hardware

Requirements

  • Currently pursuing a B.S. in Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, Aerospace or equivalent technical degree
  • Experience with C++, Python

description:
Software Development Interns - Waterloo University

Remote - Winter Session

About Brave

Brave is on a mission to protect the human right to privacy online. We’ve built a free web browser that blocks creepy ads and trackers by default, a private search engine with a truly independent index, private AI assistant, latest privacy and security features, and a private ad network (opt-in!) that directly rewards you for your attention. Already over 120 million people regularly use Brave for a faster, more private web. Millions more switch every month.

The internet is a sea of ads, hackers, and echo chambers. Big Tech makes huge profits off our data, and tells us what’s true and what’s not. Brave is fighting back. Join us!

Brave is hiring 2 Software Engineer interns this fall from Waterloo University to assist adding AI, security and privacy features to our products. 

Software Developer Co-op - Internship Role One

Contribute to the design, development, and maintenance of data-intensive systems and AI-powered services. 

Key responsibilities include:

  • Build and maintain ETL pipelines for ingesting, transforming, and loading structured and unstructured data across internal systems
  • Develop backend services and tooling in Python and TypeScript to support data processing workflows and API integrations
  • Integrate and optimize LLM inference pipelines, including prompt engineering, model serving, and evaluation of large language model outputs
  • Deploy and manage containerized workloads on Kubernetes, including writing manifests, configuring autoscaling, and troubleshooting cluster issues
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to improve data quality, pipeline reliability, and system observability

Software Developer (Privacy) Co-op - Internship Role 2

Contribute to the design, development, and shipping of privacy and security features in the Brave browser (based on Chromium).

Key responsibilities include:

  • Prototype, implement, and ship privacy-enhancing features end-to-end in C++ or Rust for the Brave browser
  • Build browser-native privacy protections privacy-enhancing permissions and anti-fingerprinting defenses
  • Navigate and contribute to an extremely large, complex codebase, applying knowledge of the Web security model and Chromium's architecture
  • Work with Web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) to develop and validate browser features
  • Collaborate async with a geographically-distributed, open source team using Git and GitHub

Working at Brave - What we offer

  • Ability to work remotely at an exciting and well-funded international startup headquartered in San Francisco
  • Cutting-edge technology, allowing you to work with state-of-the-art tools and software solutions
  • Competitive compensation of $6000.00 per month for 4 months.
  • Great international exposure and team atmosphere

If you are currently a student at Waterloo University, we would love to hear from you.  We offer flexible schedules to accommodate your studies.

description:
Kick-start your consulting career by applying your technical skills to real-world challenges in financial services.

The Role

As a Technical Consulting Intern at Capco, you’ll join our Financial Services consulting teams working with leading banks, payments providers, and wealth management firms. This internship is designed for students from a range of technical disciplines who enjoy problem-solving, exploring technology, and understanding how systems, data, and business processes work together.

You’ll gain hands-on experience supporting client engagements, collaborating with experienced consultants, and contributing to technology-driven initiatives. Whether your interests lie in software development, data analytics, systems design, or emerging technologies, you’ll have opportunities to apply your knowledge while developing practical consulting skills.

What You’ll Do

  • Support technology and digital transformation projects across banking, payments, capital markets, and wealth management.
  • Assist with analyzing technical systems, business processes, data flows, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Contribute to technical research, data analysis, dashboards, prototypes, or other technology-related deliverables.
  • Collaborate with project teams to gather requirements, document findings, and support the design of practical solutions.
  • Prepare clear presentations, documentation, and research materials to communicate technical findings and recommendations.

What We’re Looking For

  • Currently pursuing a degree or diploma in technical disciplines such as Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, Data Analytics, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • An interest in technology, analytical thinking, and solving practical problems.
  • Ability to understand technical concepts and communicate ideas clearly to different audiences.
  • Exposure through coursework, personal projects, or other experiences to programming, data analysis, technical tools, or systems and processes.
  • A collaborative approach, willingness to learn, and ability to contribute effectively in a team environment.

Bonus Points For

  • Interest in financial services, fintech, consulting, or digital transformation.
  • Familiarity with programming languages or technical tools such as Python, SQL, Java, Excel, or data visualization platforms.
  • Experience/familiarity  with LLMs or AI tools such as GPT, Codex, Gemini, or Copilot.
  • Experience with academic projects, internships, hackathons, or collaborative technical assignments.
  • Curiosity about emerging technologies, cloud platforms, automation, or modern software and data solutions.
  • Interest in exploring new technologies and applying technical knowledge to business challenges.

Why Join Capco

  • Gain hands-on experience contributing to real consulting engagements with leading financial institutions.
  • Learn from experienced consultants and develop practical technical, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Explore different areas of technology consulting, including software, data, systems, and digital transformation.
  • Work in a collaborative, non-hierarchical consulting culture where your ideas and contributions are valued.
  • Build professional connections and develop skills that support future internship and full-time career opportunities.

Compensation

The salary range for this position is CAD $23–$25 per hour.

Why This Role Is Open

We are currently hiring for this role due to an existing or newly created vacancy within our organization. This position is open as part of our ongoing business needs, and we are actively reviewing applications to fill this role with a qualified candidate who can make an immediate impact.

The posting expires on November 13, 2026.

Inclusion at Capco

We’re committed to making our recruitment process accessible and straightforward for everyone. If you need any adjustments at any stage, just let us know – we’ll be happy to help. We value each person’s unique perspective and contribution. At Capco, we believe that being yourself is your greatest strength. Our #BeYourselfAtWork culture encourages individuality and collaboration – a mindset that shapes how we work with clients and each other every day.

Use of Artificial Intelligence in Talent Acquisition

At Capco, we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support and enhance several parts of talent acquisition. This includes using AI-enabled features within LinkedIn to help source potential candidates, speeding up routine recruitment communications such as emails and creating compelling and brand-aligned job postings that accurately reflect role requirements, and AI-scheduling applications to improve the efficiency of interview coordination.

AI is used as a support tool only. All hiring decisions are made by talent acquisition and hiring teams.

Carta is the connected platform and AI-native ecosystem for private capital. Carta is looking for a Marketing Intern to join our Singapore team between January to June 2027.

Carta opened its Singapore office in 2021, and since then, has been building a world-class team to support the startup and investor ecosystem across Asia Pacific, the Middle East and Africa. 

The Marketing Intern will report up to Carta’s Head of Marketing for APAC & MEA, and get the chance to work firsthand on a range of projects, including marketing campaigns, website optimization, marketing analytics, event support and more. This role will give you the opportunity to try out the different realms of marketing and gain the necessary skill sets to jumpstart your career in B2B tech.

  • Events: Support on digital & physical marketing collateral ideation and design (presentation decks, swag) as well as provide on-the-ground support for Virtual Events & physical events
  • Other ad-hoc tasks as assigned

The Impact You will Have

As a Marketing Intern at Carta, you will be an integral part of growing the marketing function in this region. You will drive demand in the market and help oversee Carta’s growth in APAC & MEA.

About You

  • Studying Bachelors Degree in a relevant field (business, marketing)
  • Previous internship or work experience in marketing would be preferred
  • Desire to learn and work in a fast-paced environment
  • Excellent time management and organizational skills
  • Interest in B2B Marketing as well as the startup space

Nice to have:

  • Experience with marketing and sales platforms (such as Salesforce, Marketo, Figma, Google Analytics, Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads)
  • Proficiencies with Microsoft Office and/or Google Suite (GSuite)
  • Knowledge of the startup and venture capital ecosystem

 

At Carta, you’re not just an employee. You’re a builder who is creating  infrastructure that accelerates innovation and empowers more ownership. Cartans are helpful, relentless, unconventional and kind; representing Carta’s Identity Traits. They work collaboratively and cross functionally  to challenge the status quo; working towards a common goal of creating more owners in the private markets.

  • Carta uses E-Verify in the United States for employment authorization. See the E-Verify and Department of Justice websites for more details.

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Team:

Our Value Engineers (VE) are the trusted advisors for the end-to-end customer value journey, and work on the intersection of technology and business. Value Engineers partner with sales and customers to create compelling solutions and prototypes within the Celonis software to critical business problems. A great VE understands the customer, the technology, and the sales cycle making it what may be the most interesting, challenging, and fulfilling role in enterprise technology sales.

The Role:

As a Strategic Program Management Intern within the Max Success Team you will support the steering of programs that implement/execute strategic decisions from our executive management into practice. These programs span across multiple organizations, centered in Value Engineering, spanning to Product, Strategy & Ops, Ecosystem, Services, Business Apps and others. You will ensure a program’s success by building up the strategic decisions.

The work you’ll do:

  • Enable and shape data driven decision making for our management and leverage Celonis AI capabilities.
  • Design and conceptualize strategic programs (incl. data analysis).
  • Support and oversee program execution from inception to completion.
  • Coordinate and guide all involved parties in their respective streams.
  • Take ownership of specific streams, ensuring their success.
  • Identify and mitigate potential risks to ensure smooth program delivery.
  • Report to our executive management on program progress and outcomes.

The qualifications you need:

  • Student of Business Administration / Industrial Engineering / Technology & Management / Economics / or of a comparable program
  • Ability to act autonomously in high ambiguity situations
  • Stakeholder management skills
  • Project management skills
  • Financial modeling in Google Sheets
  • Confidence to present to C-level executives and larger audiences
  • Experience in consulting and highly interested in data analytics
  • Passion for technology, data, OpenAI and LLMs and the impact it can have on the world
  • This internship can be done from our Madrid Office or Munich Office. Madrid is preferred.
  • Full-time availability for at least five months starting from December/ January 26/27

What Celonis can offer you:

  • Pioneer Innovation: Work with the global leader in Process Mining and the Process Intelligence Graph to shape the future of AI-driven business operations.
  • Ownership from Day 1: Every full-time "Celonaut" is an owner, receiving Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and merit-based refresh grants.
  • Unrivaled Family Support: Benefit from our inclusive parental leave policy—24 weeks of fully paid leave for primary carers and 12 weeks for supporting carers, available from your first day of employment.
  • Work-Life Integration: Enjoy Unlimited PTO (in applicable regions) and generous PTO globally, as well as a flexible hybrid work model that balances remote focus with vibrant office collaboration.
  • Continuous Growth: Elevate your skills through our 70-20-10 learning framework, mentorship programs, and access to a dedicated learning platform.

description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available locations: 

  • Austin, TX
  • San Francisco, CA

Available Term

  • Winter (January - April 2027) 

About the Role

Cloudflare's HR/AI Transformation team makes HR work simpler and more effective. We redesign how work gets done, build internal tools (including AI tools), and run learning programs that help people adopt new ways of working. 

As our intern working on programs and processes, you'll help run those learning programs, keep our projects on track, and turn people's challenges into clear problem statements and process maps. You'll work directly with the head of AI Transformation & People Strategy, alongside HR leaders, process owners and engineers. This internship starts in January 2027 and is designed for a current student who is highly organized, writes clearly and is curious about how AI can improve the way people work.

Responsibilities

  • Plan and run our learning programs, including scheduling sessions, coordinating speakers and materials, and sending announcements and follow-ups.
  • Maintain a single, up-to-date view of all team projects, and follow up with project owners to keep work moving.
  • Write short, clear status updates for team leaders and stakeholders.
  • Meet with people across the HR function to understand their challenges, and summarize what you learn in clear problem statements.
  • Document how key processes work today, and help prepare workshops to redesign them.
  • Own one project from start to finish, with a named sponsor and a clean handoff at the end of your internship.

Requirements

  • Currently enrolled in a program studying business or similar.
  • Experience planning and managing projects or programs.
  • Strong written communication, including the ability to turn a messy conversation into a clear, simple summary.
  • Strong organization and follow-through across many people, details and deadlines.
  • Confidence working with senior leaders and reaching out to people you haven't met.
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools in your work or studies.
  • Ability to commit to a full-time (40 hours/week Monday - Friday) for a minimum 12 week internship.
  • In office 3-5 days a week.

Nice-to-Have Skills

  • Background in consulting, operations, HR or process improvement.
  • Experience with process mapping, user research or workshop facilitation.
  • Familiarity with capacity planning and project tracking tools such as Jira, Asana or Smartsheet.

Compensation
Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location.

For San Francisco Bay Area based hires: Estimated hourly rate of $27.00/hr.

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

You will collaborate with Flagship Origination Teams and fellow ML scientists/engineers to explore what is made possible by big leaps beyond the current capabilities of AI. Final work products are never just a model or a paper, they are wholistic answers to the future backwards questions we ask ourselves when originating the next big leap company.

They also work very closely with our IT Infrastructure and Cybersecurity teams on complex issues and requests. The IT Service Desk intern will start by getting trained on GCM’s end user technology stack which includes (but is not limited to) Microsoft 365, Azure Active Directory, Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows 11 administration, Active Directory, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Microsoft Endpoint Manager, Atlassian (e.g., Jira Service Desk), Cisco Meraki and our GenAI solutions. Once the intern has the required foundational knowledge, they will start supporting our users and their technology needs by handling tickets or calls. 

The summer will culminate in a presentation to the Technology leadership team reviewing the intern’s summer experience and what they learned. The team is looking for a student who is passionate about technology, excited to grow in every way, unafraid to try new things and even to fail at times along the way.

description:
HFA Intern – Summer 2027

Location: Atlanta, Georgia (Buckhead)

Duration: May 17, 2027 – July 30, 2027

Department: Hive Financial Assets (HFA)

About Us

Hive Financial Systems is a fintech company expanding financial inclusion through AI-driven lending technology. Our multi-portfolio loan management platform powers multiple lending partners serving tens of thousands of active consumers. Hive Financial Assets (HFA) is the company's private credit and investor relations arm, connecting investors to the lending portfolios that make responsible lending possible for underserved markets.

Role Overview

We're looking for a curious, detail-oriented intern to join the HFA team for the summer and provide analytics support across investor relations and capital raising. You'll work with real investor data, including CRM activity, capital raised and rolled, and investor balances, to understand how investors engage with us and help the team act on it. You'll work directly with HFA leadership, partner with Finance, Operations, and Engineering, and finish the summer with projects you can point to.

What You'll Do

  • Build investor interaction models that show how and when investors engage, using CRM activity, email, and meeting data.
  • Help design and test re-engagement ideas, and measure what works from the investor's point of view.
  • Analyze capital flows, including capital raised, rolled, and redeemed, and support forecasting of new capital.
  • Build and maintain dashboards tracking AUM, capital raised YTD, and investor engagement.
  • Help determine each investor's preferred communication method and support next-best-action recommendations for the team.
  • Provide general analytics support for investor updates, pitch materials, and leadership reporting, including checking figures for accuracy.
  • Keep investor data accurate by reconciling CRM records against internal investment schedules and flagging anomalies.

Tools You'll Use

SQL, Hex, Python, Microsoft Excel, our investor CRM, Microsoft Teams and SharePoint, and AI assistants for analysis and documentation.

Qualifications

  • Junior, senior, or master's student in Finance, Data Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Working knowledge of SQL (SELECT, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY) and strong Excel skills.
  • Some exposure to Python or R for data analysis.
  • Excellent attention to detail, especially with financial data.
  • Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain numbers to non-technical audiences.
  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with a BI tool (Hex, Power BI, Tableau, or similar).
  • Interest in private credit, alternative investments, or wealth management.
  • Basic statistics or forecasting, such as regression, time series, or A/B testing.
  • Experience with a CRM (Salesforce, Dynamics, HubSpot, or similar).

What You'll Gain

  • Hands-on experience with investor analytics and capital raising at a private credit firm.
  • Practical skills in SQL, Python, BI, and analytical modeling.
  • Mentorship from HFA leadership.
  • A portfolio-ready project presented to company leadership at the end of the summer.

Perks & Benefits

  • Regular feedback and professional development support.
  • Networking with peers and leaders across the company.
  • Flexible work arrangements (hybrid where applicable).
  • Pathways to full-time roles after graduation.

description:
Company Overview

IDMe is the next-generation digital identity wallet that simplifies how individuals securely prove their identity online. Consumers can verify their identity with IDMe once and seamlessly login across websites without having to create a new login and verify their identity again. Over 175 million users experience streamlined login and identity verification with IDMe at 22 federal agencies, 50 state government agencies, and more than 100 healthcare organizations. Over 600 consumer brands use IDMe to verify communities and user segments to honor service and build more authentic relationships. IDMe’s technology meets the federal standards for consumer authentication set by the Commerce Department and is approved as a NIST 800-63-3 IAL2 / AAL2 credential service provider by the Kantara Initiative. IDMe is committed to “No Identity Left Behind” to enable all people to have a secure digital identity. To learn more, visit https://network.id.me/.

IDMe is a full-time, in-office culture. Unless a specific job description explicitly states otherwise, all roles are on-site five days per week at one of our offices in McLean, VA; Mountain View, CA; New York City, NY; or Tampa, FL. Certain roles — such as field-based sales or other remote-by-design positions — may have different work arrangements as noted in their individual postings.

At IDMe, we embrace the thoughtful use of AI tools in our daily work and there are even occasions where we leverage AI in our hiring process. However, during the interview process, we want to understand your individual skills and experiences. Therefore, we have guidelines on how AI can be appropriately used during your application and interviews which can be found here.

About the role 

IDMe is hiring a Product Security Engineering Intern for Summer 2027. You will join the Product Security team, which keeps the platform that verifies identities for over 156 million people across 21 federal agencies, 50 state agencies, and more than 600 businesses secure by design. 

This is a hands-on engineering internship, not a shadowing program. You will own a scoped project from start to finish, ship real improvements to how we build and run software, and present your results to security and engineering leadership at the end of the summer. 

Location: Mountain View, California 

What you'll do 

  • Partner with engineering teams on threat models and security design reviews for new features and services. 
  • Triage findings from static analysis (SAST), dependency scanning (SCA), secrets detection, and container scanning, and help engineers fix them. 
  • Build or improve automation that brings security checks into CI/CD pipelines and developer workflows. 
  • Help assess and improve the security posture of our cloud environments, including cloud security posture management (CSPM) and container runtime tooling. 
  • Perform focused code reviews and security testing against industry-standard and internal security frameworks and requirements. 
  • Write clear documentation, secure coding guidance, and runbooks that engineers will actually use. 
  • Deliver an intern capstone project and present it to the team at the end of the summer. 
  • Your capstone will go deep on one or two of the areas above rather than touching all of them; your mentor will help you pick the one with the clearest scope and the most direct line to a shipped improvement. 

What we're looking for

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Computer Engineering, or a related field. 
  • Working knowledge of common web application vulnerabilities (injection, XSS, broken authentication, access control flaws) and how to prevent them. 
  • Familiarity with Git, the Linux command line, and basic networking concepts (HTTP, TLS, DNS). 
  • Curiosity, a builder's mindset, and the ability to explain technical risk clearly to engineers who are not security specialists. 
  • Must be authorized to work in the United States. 
  • Must be able to pass a standard background check, consistent with our work for government agencies and regulated industries. 

Nice to have 

  • Experience with a major cloud provider, containers, or container orchestration. * Hands-on experience with application security testing and scanning tools. 
  • CTF participation, bug bounty findings, a security club, open-source contributions, or a home lab you can talk about. 
  • Coursework or projects in applied cryptography, identity and access management, or authentication protocols (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML). 
  • Interest in identity, fraud prevention, or privacy. 

What you'll gain 

  • A dedicated mentor on the Product Security team and regular 1:1s with security leadership. 
  • Real-world experience securing a high-scale identity platform that operates under strict compliance requirements (NIST 800-63, FedRAMP, SOC 2). 
  • Practical depth in application security, cloud security, and DevSecOps that maps directly to full-time security engineering roles. 
  • A shipped project and a final presentation you can point to in future interviews.

The annual base salary listed does not include a company bonus, incentive for sales roles, equity and benefits

  • Translate classroom experience into practical application during the internship

  • Learning best practice techniques for calling and emailing prospects

description:
Your Impact at LILA

Our team works on AI methods for therapeutic protein design, with a tight loop between computation and the wet lab. A co-op could take on either of two tracks, or a mix of both. (1) Generative models and protein design pipelines: build, benchmark, and improve methods for designing proteins (such as antibodies and minibinders), with candidates tested in our lab so results are grounded in experimental data. (2) AI agents for protein design campaigns: build and evaluate agents that help plan campaign strategy (target and epitope selection, choosing methods and settings), execute campaigns (launching design and filtering runs, diagnosing failures, adapting the next round), and reason over biological priors from the literature alongside the outputs of domain-specific models. Either way, the co-op would own a well-scoped project, ship code and analyses that feed real design decisions and scientific outcomes.

What You'll Be Building

  • Develop, evaluate, and apply agentic systems for protein design and/or deep generative models for protein design.

What You'll Need to Succeed

  • Strong python and and computational science background.
  • Experience with coding agents.
  • Experience with machine learning for molecular design

Bonus Points For

  • Experience with customizing agents, building harnesses, or using agents for scientific applications
  • Solid technical understand and experience with generative models.

About LILA

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai.

Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply.

We’re All In

Lila Sciences is committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

Information you provide during your application process will be handled in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Policy.

A Note to Agencies

Lila Sciences does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than candidates. The submission of unsolicited resumes by recruitment or staffing agencies to Lila Sciences or its employees is strictly prohibited unless contacted directly by Lila Science’s internal Talent Acquisition team. Any resume submitted by an agency in the absence of a signed agreement will automatically become the property of Lila Sciences, and Lila Sciences will not owe any referral or other fees with respect thereto.

description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila's SCADA system spans cloud and on-premise infrastructure: Ignition gateways on EC2, a historian on RDS PostgreSQL, MQTT brokers, and edge nodes at each site. Today no single view shows the health of all of it, so the team learns about failures from users rather than from monitoring.

As a co-op on the Hardware & Controls Engineering team, you will build that view: a live connectivity diagram showing how every piece connects and which links are up, backed by dashboards covering database, gateway, and edge node health. The work is read-only end to end, with read-only AWS access and SELECT-only database access, so you can explore the full system safely.

You will be based at our Alewife site in Cambridge, working alongside controls engineers and the IT/OT team. Expect wide exposure across AWS, Linux, industrial networking, Ignition, and data visualization, and a clear picture of how an industrial SCADA system fits together end to end.

What You'll Be Building

description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila Sciences builds AI systems that accelerate discovery across the physical and life sciences. Within Physical Sciences AI, we work with experimental teams to build autonomous discovery agents that decide which experiments Lila's AI Science Factories should run next.

Real scientific campaigns rarely look like textbook optimization problems. A single campaign can mix large discrete choices (which components, which recipe) with continuous settings (amounts, temperatures, times), pursue several objectives under hard constraints, and draw on evidence from literature and characterization data. Every experiment costs real time and materials. Off-the-shelf methods often struggle here, and they ignore the domain structure that could guide the search.

As a Bayesian Methods Co-Op, you will work alongside research scientists and engineers on a focused project within one broad question: how AI systems can make better experimental decisions. Depending on your background, that could mean building agents that choose the next experiment, testing when in-context learners can be trusted as decision-makers, or developing Bayesian strategies for tight experimental budgets. Your methods will be tested against live campaigns.

What You'll Be Building

  • Design and benchmark experiment-selection strategies that balance exploration and exploitation under realistic budgets
  • Build autonomous discovery agents that propose the next experiment from surrogate models
  • Develop in-context learning approaches inspired by Bayesian inference, evaluating calibration and robustness
  • Run retrospective and live evaluations on active campaign data with clear baselines and metrics
  • Present findings to ML and experimental teams, with the option to contribute to a publication

What You'll Need to Succeed

  • Pursuing a Master's or PhD in statistics, ML, CS, operations research, applied math, or a quantitative science
  • Solid grounding in Bayesian inference and decision making, including priors and posterior predictive distributions
  • Research experience in Gaussian processes, Bayesian optimization, bandits, reinforcement learning, or probabilistic modeling
  • Strong Python skills with PyTorch and probabilistic libraries such as Pyro, PyMC, or BoTorch
  • Comfort working with small, noisy, and heterogeneous datasets
  • Clear communication with both ML and experimental collaborators

Bonus Points For

  • Applying these methods to real problems in materials science, chemistry, or another physical science
  • Familiarity with in-context learning as implicit Bayesian inference, meta-learning, or prior-data fitted networks
  • Optimization over categorical or combinatorial spaces, including mixed-variable, multi-objective, or batch settings

  • Training models on multimodal scientific data such as text, images, spectra, or simulations

Your Impact at LILA

The PS AI team sits at the intersection of Physical Sciences R&D and AI/ML. Lila runs high-throughput experiments across electrochemistry, formulations, and advanced materials, generating rich datasets that demand more than black-box models.

As a Co-Op focused on AI-driven equation discovery, you will develop and benchmark methods that extract interpretable governing equations directly from that data. Discovered equations reveal the underlying physics, make predictions explainable, and serve as mechanistic building blocks for digital twins and closed-loop optimization.

You will work alongside PS AI researchers and physical scientists, helping shape how Lila turns experimental data into scientific understanding at scale.

  • Translate open scientific questions into concrete problems with datasets, baselines, and success criteria

About Moment Energy

Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it.

Energy should be free.  Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone.

The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy.

Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact.

We were told second-life batteries would never be safe enough or scalable enough. We didn’t argue, we engineered the solution. Today, Moment Energy delivers 5x the energy density and holds the certifications required to deploy energy independence at scale.

Now is the moment. Join us.
